title: B2-12 · Facts and opinions: language markers

blocks.text: B2-12 · Facts and opinions: language markers
Lesson overview

This unit closes the work of the module B2.2 and transforms it into a method. In each text there are facts (verifiables), statements (attributed to someone), interpretations (linking facts) and opinions (value judgments). The language signals them with precise markers, but sometimes it confuses them on purpose: "It is evident that """ """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" In this unit you learn to recognize the markers of each category, to expose opinions disguised as facts, to distinguish established cause and hypothetical cause, and to build a note of analysis in English that separates the four levels. Three weeks, in parallel with ARZ-01 and the beginning of EGY-16.

rows: B2 · Module B2.2 Attribution and certainty
B2-07 → B2-11; INT-01 (assignment, prudence); B2-04 (date, decision, interpretation)
16–18 hours · three weeks (weeks 200–202), plus the ARZ/EGY track in separate blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Reference Grammar (G)71), four color markers, voice synthesis scripts, tutor sessions
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. categorize the sentences of a text in facts, statements, interpretations and opinions, with the markers which the report;
2. recognising the views presented as facts ( ⁧مِنَ الوَاضِحِ أَنَّ⁩ , ⁧الحَقِيقَةُ أَنَّ⁩ , ⁧مِمَّا يَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّ⁩ );
3. distinguish a causal relationship established by a proven one;
4. identify what a text does not say (lacune) and what it would take to verify it;
5. write a note of analysis in English with the four separate levels.
Three-week plan.

The criterion. Always ask yourself: "Who might not agree with this phrase?" If someone, with reasonable arguments, might not be, it is an opinion or an interpretation, even if the text presents it as obvious.

8. The analytical note
A note of analysis (in English) on an Arabic article follows a fixed structure. Here's the outline of the course:

rows: testata, date, author, type of text (news, analysis, opinion), link and date of consultation
the names of the newspapers as they appear, with transliteration
what the text presents as a fact, with the source
indicate whether the source is cited
who says what, with the Arabic verb
the journalist or ascribed; formulas and connotations
6 · Lacks and elements to be verified
what is lacking, what has not been possible

The formulas disguised. Read with the tutor, first in neutral tone and then in emphatic tone: mina l-wāḍiḥi anna... · al- ḥaqīqatu Anna... · wa-hāḏā yuṯbitu Anna... Known as the emphasis increases the effect of "truth": this is precisely why they should be read carefully. ⁧تَزَامُن⁩ . tazāmun: sound z, accent on the second long syllable (-zā-).

Notes of use. ⁧يَعُودُ إِلَى⁩ has two senses: temporal (-) ⁧يَعُودُ المَبْنَى إِلَى القَرْنِ التَّاسِعَ عَشَرَ⁩ ) and causal (-) is due to - (-)). ⁧وَاقِعَة⁩ (pl. ⁧وَقَائِع⁩ ) is the fact in a legal or chronical sense; ⁧حَقِيقَة⁩ is the truth, but also is done in general contexts ( ⁧حَقِيقَةٌ عِلْمِيَّةٌ⁩ (a scientific fact) ⁧أَثْبَتَ⁩ is a strong verb: in the press it is often the author's thesis, not a true demonstration.
